tagline: Up the copper lode to the end of US 41.
intro: Out of Houghton, US 41 crosses Portage Lake on the lift bridge, runs through Hancock and climbs Quincy Hill to the mine at the top. From there it follows the middle of the Keweenaw Peninsula through Calumet, once the center of Michigan copper, and on past the old mine sites at Phoenix and Delaware to Copper Harbor at the tip.
Past Fort Wilkins the highway stops at a cul-de-sac. Miami is 1,990 miles back down the same road. The stretch from Houghton up to Phoenix was laid out in 1864 as the Military Road to Fort Wilkins.

moments.title: Portage Lake Lift Bridge
moments.text: The heaviest and widest double-decked lift bridge in the world, the only land link to the north half of the Keweenaw, with snowmobiles on its lower deck in winter.

moments.title: Quincy Mine
moments.text: Its No. 2 shaft runs 9,260 feet down the lode, and a cog railway takes visitors to the seventh level, as deep as the groundwater now allows.

moments.title: Brockway Mountain Drive
moments.text: Out-of-work copper miners built it by hand in 1933 along the Keweenaw Fault, 720 feet above Lake Superior, where Isle Royale shows about 50 miles out on a clear day.

practical: Brockway Mountain Drive is not plowed and is closed to cars in winter, when it serves as a snowmobile trail.
